To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
JSRV, ENVT-1 and ENTV- 2 are all active promoters of gene expression in the distal respiratory tract of mice but that only ENTV induces tumors in the nasal cavity.
the JSRV, the ENTVs, and the AAV-ENV vectors are expressed only in the alveolar type 2 cells and the nasal epitheliam, respectively.
the ENTV-2 and JSRV LTR promoters are active in the nasal and alveolar epithelium of mice, but the JSRV LTR promoter is more active in the alveolar epithelial cells than in nasal epithelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the induction of nasal tumors in mice using AAV vectors expressing ENTV genes.
the study of viruses that cause lung cancer in sheep and goats, and our findings have implications for the use of retroviral promoters in gene therapy.
the development of gene therapy vectors that can be used to target the distal airspaces of the lung and nasal epithelia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the LTRs of JSRV and EN TV are tissue specific in the mouse and that the JSRV Env protein is sufficient to induce tumors in the lower respiratory tract of the mouse, whereas the ENTV Env protein is not sufficient for nasal tumor induction in the mouse.
the JSRV and the ENTV LTRS drive expression in all epithelial cells of the respiratory tract of the mouse.

the JSRV, but not the ENTV, LTR promoter drives gene expression in the distal epithelial airway cells of mice, and that the JSRV LTR, but not the LTR of either ENTV, is sufficient to induce tumors in the alveolar region of the lungs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LTRs of ENTV and JSRV can drive gene expression in all airway and nasal epithelial cells of mice, but they are not sufficient to induce tumor development in these cells.
all three retroviral LTRs are active in all airways, but the JSRV LTR is the strongest promoter and the ENTV-2 is the weakest promoter.

the JSRV and the closely related ENTV-1 induce tumors in the lower airways and the nasal cavity, respectively, in their natural hosts, but only induce tumors in the distalmost airway of the lungs when introduced into mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the JSRV and the two ENTVs have very distinct tissue tropisms and that the JSRV LTR is the most active promoter of the three.
the LTRs and the Env protein of JSRV and ENVT are not sufficient to induce tumors in the upper respiratory tract of mice.
the ENTV LTRS do not appear to be sufficient for tumor induction, and the JSRV LTR is not sufficient to induce tumors in the alveolar region.
